sanskrit: muñcāmi tvā haviṣā jīvanāya kam ajñātayakṣmād uta rājayakṣmāt | grāhir jagrāha yadi vaitad enaṁ tasyā indrāgnī pra mumuktam enam ||
english: I release you with oblation for the sake of life, from the unknown consumption and from the royal consumption (rājayakṣma). If the Grāhī (the seizing demon) has seized him, from her, O Indra and Agni, set this one free.

sanskrit: yadi kṣitāyur yadi vā pareto yadi mṛtyor antikaṁ nīta eva | tam ā harāmi nirṛter upasthād aspārṣam enaṁ śataśāradāya ||
english: Whether his life-span is exhausted, whether he has already departed, whether he has been led to the very threshold of Death — I bring him back from the lap of Nirṛti; I have rescued him for a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣeṇa śataśāradena śatāyuṣā haviṣāhārṣam enam | śataṁ yathe maṁ śarado nayātīndro viśvasya duritasya pāram ||
english: With the thousand-eyed oblation that brings a hundred autumns and a hundred years of life, I have fetched him back — that Indra may lead this man through a hundred autumns, beyond all misfortune.

sanskrit: śataṁ jīva śarado vardhamānaḥ śataṁ hemantāñ chatam u vasantān | śatam indrāgnī savitā bṛhaspatiḥ śatāyuṣā haviṣe mam punar duḥ ||
english: Live a hundred autumns, growing in strength; live a hundred winters, a hundred springs! May Indra, Agni, Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati restore this man again with an oblation that bestows a hundred years of life.

sanskrit: āhārṣaṁ tvāvidaṁ tvā punar āgāḥ punarnava | sarvāṅga sarvaṁ te cakṣuḥ sarvam āyuś ca te 'vidam ||
english: I have brought you back; I have found you; you have come again, renewed. O whole-limbed one, all your sight have I found for you, and all your life-span.

sanskrit: brahmaṇāgniḥ saṁvidāno rakṣohā bādhatām itaḥ | amīvā yas te garbhaṁ durṇāmā yonim āśaye ||
english: May Agni, the slayer of demons, acting in concert with sacred prayer (brahman), drive away from here the disease called Amīvā, of evil name, that lies lurking in your womb and endangers your embryo.

sanskrit: yas te garbham amīvā durṇāmā yonim āśaye | agniṣ ṭam brahmaṇā saha niṣ kravyādam anīnaśat ||
english: That Amīvā of evil name which lies lurking in your womb threatening your embryo — Agni together with brahman has driven out that flesh-eating demon.

sanskrit: yas te hanti patayantaṁ niṣatsnuṁ yaḥ sarīsṛpam | jātaṁ yas te jighāṁsati tam ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Him who kills the (embryo) that flies about, that settles in the womb, that creeps — him who seeks to destroy the child once born — that one we drive away from here.

sanskrit: yas ta ūrū viharaty antarā dampatī śaye | yoniṁ yo antar āreḻhi tam ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Him who forces apart your thighs when husband and wife lie together, who licks inside the womb — that one we drive away from here.

sanskrit: yas tvā bhrātā patir bhūtvā jāro bhūtvā nipadyate | prajāṁ yas te jighāṁsati tam ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Him who, having become as a brother or a husband, or as a lover, lies down upon you — who seeks to destroy your offspring — that one we drive away from here.

sanskrit: yas tvā svapnena tamasā mohayitvā nipadyate | prajāṁ yas te jighāṁsati tam ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Him who, having deluded you through sleep and darkness, lies down upon you — who seeks to destroy your offspring — that one we drive away from here.

sanskrit: akṣībhyāṁ te nāsikābhyāṁ karṇābhyāṁ chubukād adhi | yakṣmaṁ śīrṣaṇyam mastiṣkāj jihvāyā vi vṛhāmi te ||
english: From your eyes, from your nostrils, from your ears, from your chin — the head-disease (śīrṣaṇya yakṣma) from your brain and from your tongue — I tear it out for you.

sanskrit: grīvābhyas ta uṣṇihābhyaḥ kīkasābhyo anūkyāt | yakṣmaṁ doṣaṇyam aṁsābhyām bāhubhyāṁ vi vṛhāmi te ||
english: From your neck, from your nape (uṣṇihā), from your vertebrae (kīkasā), from the spine (anūkya) — the shoulder-disease (doṣaṇya yakṣma) from your shoulders and from your arms — I tear it out for you.

sanskrit: āntrebhyas te gudābhyo vaniṣṭhor hṛdayād adhi | yakṣmam matasnābhyāṁ yaknaḥ plāśibhyo vi vṛhāmi te ||
english: From your intestines, from your rectum, from the vaniṣṭhu (belly-region), and from above your heart — the disease from your kidneys (matasnā), from your liver, from your spleen — I tear it out for you.

sanskrit: ūrubhyāṁ te aṣṭhīvadbhyām pārṣṇibhyām prapadābhyām | yakṣmaṁ śroṇibhyām bhāsadād bhaṁsaso vi vṛhāmi te ||
english: From your thighs, from your knees, from your heels, from the balls of your feet — the disease from your hips, from the buttocks, from the hinder parts — I tear it out for you.

sanskrit: mehanād vanaṁkaraṇāl lomabhyas te nakhebhyaḥ | yakṣmaṁ sarvasmād ātmanas tam idaṁ vi vṛhāmi te ||
english: From the organ of urination, from the groin (vanaṁkaraṇa), from your body hair, from your nails — the disease from your entire self — this one I tear out for you.

sanskrit: aṅgād-aṅgāl lomno-lomno jātam parvaṇi-parvaṇi | yakṣmaṁ sarvasmād ātmanas tam idaṁ vi vṛhāmi te ||
english: That which has arisen from limb to limb, from hair to hair, from joint to joint — the disease from your entire self — this one I tear out for you.

sanskrit: apehi manasas pate 'pa krāma paraś cara | paro nirṛtyā ā cakṣva bahudhā jīvato manaḥ ||
english: Depart, O lord of the mind; step away, go far off! Speak of the manifold mind of the living man from beyond Nirṛti (Dissolution).

sanskrit: bhadraṁ vai varaṁ vṛṇate bhadraṁ yuñjanti dakṣiṇam | bhadraṁ vaivasvate cakṣur bahutrā jīvato manaḥ ||
english: Auspicious indeed is the boon they choose; auspicious is the right hand they yoke. Auspicious is the eye of Vaivasvata (Yama); manifold is the mind of the living man.

sanskrit: yad āśasā niḥśasābhiśasoparima jāgrato yat svapantaḥ | agnir viśvāny apa duṣkṛtāny ajuṣṭāny āre asmad dadhātu ||
english: Whatever wrong we have incurred through hope, through imprecation, through slander, while awake or while asleep — may Agni place all evil deeds, all things displeasing, far away from us.

sanskrit: yad indra brahmaṇas pate 'bhidrohaṁ carāmasi | pracetā na āṅgiraso dviṣatām pātv aṁhasaḥ ||
english: O Indra, O lord of sacred prayer, whatever treachery we commit — may the wise Āṅgirasa guard us from the sin of enemies.

sanskrit: ajaiṣmādyāsanāma cābhūmānāgaso vayam | jāgratsvapaṇaḥ saṁkalpaḥ pāpo yaṁ dviṣmas taṁ sa ṛcchatu yo no dveṣṭi tam ṛcchatu ||
english: We have conquered today; we shall conquer; we have become free from sin. The evil of waking thought and dreaming, of evil intention — let it befall him whom we hate; let it befall him who hates us.

sanskrit: devāḥ kapota iṣito yad icchan dūto nirṛtyā idam ājagāma | tasmā arcāma kṛṇavāma niṣkṛtiṁ śaṁ no astu dvipade śaṁ catuṣpade ||
english: O gods, this dove, sent purposefully and desiring something, has come here as a messenger of Nirṛti (the goddess of ruin). For him let us sing and perform the rite of expiation. May there be welfare for our two-footed (creatures), welfare for our four-footed (creatures).

sanskrit: śivaḥ kapota iṣito no astv anāgā devāḥ śakuno gṛheṣu | agnir hi vipro juṣatāṁ havir naḥ pari hetiḥ pakṣiṇī no vṛṇaktu ||
english: May the dove sent (as an omen) be auspicious to us; may the bird be free of sin in our houses, O gods. May Agni, the wise one, accept our oblation; may the winged shaft (of Nirṛti) turn away from us.

sanskrit: hetiḥ pakṣiṇī na dabhāty asmān āṣṭryām padaṁ kṛṇute agnidhāne | śaṁ no gobhyaś ca puruṣebhyaś cāstu mā no hiṁsīd iha devāḥ kapotaḥ ||
english: May the winged shaft not harm us; it places its foot on the fire-holder (āṣṭryā). May there be welfare for our cattle and our people; may the dove not injure us here, O gods.

sanskrit: yad ulūko vadati mogham etad yat kapotaḥ padam agnau kṛṇoti | yasya dūtaḥ prahita eṣa etat tasmai yamāya namo astu mṛtyave ||
english: What the owl cries — that is in vain; and what the dove's foot touches in the fire. He whose messenger this one has been sent — to that Yama, to Death, let there be homage.

sanskrit: ṛcā kapotaṁ nudata praṇodam iṣam madantaḥ pari gāṁ nayadhvam | saṁyopayanto duritāni viśvā hitvā na ūrjam pra patāt patiṣṭhaḥ ||
english: With the Ṛc (verse) drive away the dove, drive it off; exulting in refreshment, lead the cow around. Having closed off all evil, let the most excellent one fly forth, abandoning his strength for us.

sanskrit: ṛṣabham mā samānānāṁ sapatnānāṁ viṣāsahim | hantāraṁ śatrūṇāṁ kṛdhi virājaṁ gopatiṁ gavām ||
english: Make me the bull among equals, the one who overcomes rivals, the slayer of enemies, the sovereign (virāj), the lord of cattle.

sanskrit: aham asmi sapatnahendra ivāriṣṭo akṣataḥ | adhaḥ sapatnā me pador ime sarve abhiṣṭhitāḥ ||
english: I am the slayer of rivals, unharmed and uninjured like Indra. These rivals are all trodden down beneath my feet.

sanskrit: atraiva vo 'pi nahyāmy ubhe ārtnī iva jyayā | vācas pate ni ṣedhemān yathā mad adharaṁ vadān ||
english: Right here I tie you (rivals) together, as both ends (of a bow) are tied by the bowstring. O lord of speech, silence these men so that they may speak beneath me.

sanskrit: abhibhūr aham āgamaṁ viśvakarmeṇa dhāmnā | ā vaś cittam ā vo vratam ā vo 'haṁ samitiṁ dade ||
english: I have come as the overpowering one, with the power of Viśvakarman. I take possession of your minds, your vows; I take possession of your assembly.

sanskrit: yogakṣemaṁ va ādāyāham bhūyāsam uttama ā vo mūrdhānam akramīm | adhaspadān ma ud vadate maṇḍūkā ivoda kān maṇḍūkā udakād iva ||
english: Having taken your welfare and prosperity, may I become the highest; I have stepped upon your heads. Speak up to me from beneath my feet, as frogs (croak) up toward the water, as frogs (speak) from the water.

sanskrit: tubhye dam indra pari ṣicyate madhu tvaṁ sutasya kalaśasya rājasi | tvaṁ rayim puruvīrām u nas kṛdhi tvaṁ tapaḥ paritapyājayaḥ svaḥ ||
english: For you, O Indra, this sweet liquor is poured out; you reign over the pressed (soma) and the jar. Grant us wealth with many heroes; through fervent ardour you have won the heavenly light (svar).

sanskrit: svarjitam mahi mandānam andhasoa havāmahe pari śakraṁ sutāṁ upa | imaṁ no yajñam iha bodhy ā gahi spṛdho jayantam maghavānam īmahe ||
english: We call upon the mighty, greatly exhilarating, heaven-winning (Soma), around the mighty Śakra (Indra) where it is pressed. O be aware of our sacrifice here, come hither; we beseech the bountiful one (Maghavan) who is victorious in contests.

sanskrit: somasya rājño varuṇasya dharmaṇi bṛhaspater anumatyā u śarmaṇi | tavāham adya maghavann upastutau dhātar vidhātaḥ kalaśāṁ abhakṣayam ||
english: In the ordinance of King Soma and of Varuṇa, with the approval of Bṛhaspati, in his shelter — in your praise today, O Maghavan, O Dhātṛ, O Vidhātṛ, I have drunk the jars (of Soma).

sanskrit: prasūto bhakṣam akaraṁ carāv api stomaṁ cemam prathamaḥ sūrir un mṛje | sute sātena yady āgamaṁ vām prati viśvāmitrajamadagnī dame ||
english: Urged on, I have taken my share; I have partaken of the food; I, the first sage, polish up this hymn of praise. If with the pressed (Soma) and with (the prize) won I have come to the house of you two — Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni.

sanskrit: vātasya nu mahimānaṁ rathasya rujann eti stanayann asya ghoṣaḥ | divispṛg yāty aruṇāni kṛṇvann uto eti pṛthivyā reṇum asyan ||
english: Now the greatness of the Wind's chariot — its sound goes crashing and thundering; it touches the sky, turning all things ruddy, and it goes stirring up the dust of the earth.

sanskrit: sam prerate anu vātasya viṣṭhā ainaṁ gacchanti samanam na yoṣāḥ | tābhiḥ sayuk sarathaṁ deva īyate 'sya viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā ||
english: Along with (the Wind) the troops of the Vātasya (Wind's hosts) rush together; the women go toward him like (going to) an assembly. Yoked together with them, on the same chariot, this god travels — the king of this whole world of beings.

sanskrit: antarikṣe pathibhir īyamāno na ni viśate katamac canāhaḥ | apāṁ sakhā prathamajā ṛtāvā kva svij jātaḥ kuta ā babhūva ||
english: Traveling through the middle air by his paths, he does not rest in any place on any day. The firstborn friend of waters, the guardian of cosmic order (ṛtavan) — where indeed was he born? From whence did he come to be?

sanskrit: ātmā devānām bhuvanasya garbho yathāvaśaṁ carati deva eṣaḥ | ghoṣā id asya śṛṇvire na rūpaṁ tasmai vātāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: The breath (ātman) of the gods, the embryo of the world — this god moves as he wills. His sounds alone are heard, not his form. To that Vāta (Wind) let us offer homage with oblation.

sanskrit: mayobhūr vāto abhi vātū srā ūrjasvātīr oṣadhīr ā riśantām | pīvasvatīr jīvadha nyāḥ pibantu avasāya padvate rudra mṛḻa ||
english: May the bliss-giving Wind blow upon (the cows); may the vigorous plants satisfy them. May the fat-uddered ones, bringing life in their grain, drink; O Rudra, show grace to the quadruped for the good of the settlement.

sanskrit: yāḥ sarūpā virūpā ekarūpā yāsām agnir iṣṭyā nāmāni veda | yā aṅgirasa tapase ha cakrus tābhyaḥ parjanya mahi śarma yaccha ||
english: Those (cows) of like form, of differing form, of one form — those whose names Agni knows by sacred rite — those which the Aṅgirasas employed here for penance: to them, O Parjanya, grant great shelter.

sanskrit: yā deveṣu tanvam airayanta yāsāṁ somo viśvā rūpāṇi veda | tā asmabhyam payasā pinvamānāḥ prajāvatīr indra goṣṭhe rirīhi ||
english: Those (cows) that have displayed their bodies among the gods, all of whose forms Soma knows — those, swelling with milk for us, rich in offspring — let them flow, O Indra, in the cow-stall.

sanskrit: prajāpatir mahyam etā rarāṇo viśvair devaiḥ pitṛbhiḥ saṁvidānaḥ | śivāḥ satīr upa no goṣṭham ākas tāsāṁ vayam prajayā saṁ sadema ||
english: Prajāpati, having gifted these to me, acting in accord with all the gods and ancestors — auspicious as they are, has led them into our cow-stall. Together with their offspring may we sit down with them.

sanskrit: vibhrāḍ bṛhat pibatu somyam madhv āyur dadhad yajñapatāv avihrutam | vātajūto yo abhirakṣati tmanā prajāḥ pupoṣa purudhā vi rājati ||
english: Let the great Resplendent One (Sūrya) drink the sweet Soma-beverage, placing unimpaired life in the lord of the sacrifice. Urged by the Wind, he who guards (creation) by his own power — he has nourished creatures and shines widely in manifold ways.

sanskrit: vibhrāḍ bṛhat subhṛtaṁ vājasātamaṁ dharman divo dharuṇe satyam arpitam | amitrahā vṛtrahā dasyuhaṁtamaṁ jyotir jajñe asurahā sapatnāhā ||
english: The great Resplendent One, well-borne, most winning of prizes, established in truth on the foundation of heaven's ordinance — the slayer of non-allies, slayer of Vṛtra, most potent slayer of Dasyus — this light was born, slayer of Asuras and of rivals.

sanskrit: idaṁ śreṣṭhaṁ jyotiṣāṁ jyotir uttamaṁ viśvajid dhanajid ucyate bṛhat | viśvabhrāḍ bhrājo mahi sūryo dṛśa uru paprathe saha ojo acyutam ||
english: This is the best of lights, the highest light; called the Great, the all-conquering, wealth-conquering. Sūrya — the all-illumining, great in splendour, great to behold — has spread widely together with unfaltering might.

sanskrit: vibhrajañ jyotiṣā svar agacchor ocanam divaḥ | yene mā viśvā bhuvanāny ābhṛtā viśvakarmaṇā viśvadaivyāvatā ||
english: Blazing with light, the sun went to the shining realm (svar), to the luminous realm of heaven — that (light) by which all these worlds are upheld through the all-doing (Viśvakarman), protected by all the divine powers.
